name: North American F-86 Sabre
summary: Iconic swept-wing day fighter of the Korean War; a dozen or so privately owned Sabres fly in the US as warbirds.

wings: Mid-mounted wing swept back about 35 degrees
engines: Single turbojet fed by a round nose intake
One round tailpipe at the rear
fuselage: Bubble canopy on a long, slim fuselage
Pointed nose with the intake below the nose cone
tail: Swept horizontal tail mounted lower than the MiG-15's

tellTales: Round nose intake and swept wings on a slim jet fighter
Bubble canopy and tall swept fin
Swept horizontal tail mounted low on the fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The Hunter has wing-root intakes and a pointed nose; the Sabre has a nose intake.
The T-33 has straight wings with tip tanks; the Sabre has swept wings.
The F-5 is a twin-engine supersonic fighter with side intakes; the Sabre is a single-engine jet with a nose intake.
